items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The block decomposition and isometric tail/right blocks imply the stated squared Frobenius bound. The Lean projector identity Q(Q^T AΩ)=AΩ is exactly range(AΩ)⊆range(Q) for orthonormal Q; IsUnit(Ω1 Ω1^T) is the full-row-rank condition. The competitor and truncated variant are genuine strengthenings, not substitute assumptions.
items.informal_at_review: If $\operatorname{range}(A\Omega) \subseteq \operatorname{range}(Q)$ and $\Omega_1 = V_1^\top\Omega$ has full row rank, then $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2 \le \|\Sigma_2\|_F^2 + \|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F^2.$$
hypotheses_at_review: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ with block SVD $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$
items.conclusion_at_review: $\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2 \le \|\Sigma_2\|_F^2 + \|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F^2$

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: Lean uses zero-based σ ℓ and Ico k ℓ, which exactly translate the one-based σ_(ℓ+1) and sum from k+1 to ℓ. Denominator positivity is supplied by k<ℓ. The second finite-tail version requires t>0, 4k≤t, ℓ=(t+1)/2 and ℓ≤N; zero-padding handles later singular values.
items.informal_at_review: $\sigma_{\ell+1}^2 \le \frac{1}{\ell-k}\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$; that is, for $t \ge 4k$, $$\sigma_{\lceil t/2\rceil+1}^2 \le \frac{4}{t}\cdot\mathrm{OPT}^2.$$
items.conclusion_at_review: $\sigma_{\ell+1}^2 \le \frac{1}{\ell-k}\sum_{i=k+1}^{\ell}\sigma_i^2$, and $\sigma_{\lceil t/2\rceil+1}^2 \le \frac{4}{t}\cdot\mathrm{OPT}^2$ with $\mathrm{OPT}^2 = \sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The projector power inequality uses Hermitian idempotence and q a natural number. The residual corollary has HasOrthonormalCols Q, and the rooted endpoint uses exponent 1/(2q+1); q=0 is included. The proof is stronger than the sketch-generated case and does not claim a realization theorem for orth.
items.informal_at_review: For $Y = (AA^\top)^qA\Omega$ and $Q = \operatorname{orth}(Y)$: $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\| \le \|(I-QQ^\top)(AA^\top)^qA\|^{1/(2q+1)}.$$ Turns the RSVD bound into a bound with $\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1}$ decay.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The raw Moore–Penrose generalized Nyström endpoint uses independent actual Gaussian sketches. Its second-sketch threshold uses min(rank A,t)+2≤s and its dimension factor min(rank A,t), a useful refinement of the human t-based factor. The exact-rank branch gives recovery when the sketch widths span the rank; older completion assembly endpoints must not be used as standalone law-free guarantees.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The indexed complex and real finite-history law endpoints realize the actual adaptive diagonal-proportional process, including absorbing zero residuals. The relative-tail step budget and zero-tail branch match the human clauses, and arbitrary ε>0 is allowed. The eta-independent source branch is explicitly not claimed. Positive-tail assumptions avoid division by the zero trace.
items.informal_at_review: For the actual adaptive diagonal-proportional complex Cholesky process, the retained relative spectral-tail budget gives expected real-trace error at most 1+epsilon times the optimum tail. Eta is the relative tail, and zero residuals are absorbing.
hypotheses_at_review: $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ is PSD, $1\le r\le n$, $\varepsilon>0$ and $a=\sum_{j>r}\lambda_j(A)$ with eigenvalues indexed from one

At a nonzero residual R, choose i with probability $\operatorname{Re}R_{ii}/\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}R$ and update $R\leftarrow R-R_{:,i}R_{:,i}^*/R_{ii}$; zero diagonal entries have probability zero and R=0 remains zero
For a>0, set $\eta=a/\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}A$ and take $k\ge r/\varepsilon+r\log(1/(\varepsilon\eta))$ pivots; for a=0 take k>=r
items.conclusion_at_review: The actual finite adaptive expectation satisfies $\mathbb E\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}R_k\le(1+\varepsilon)a$. Every positive epsilon is covered, including a negative displayed step budget when the initial error is already small. For a=0 the residual vanishes almost surely after at most r positive pivots. For h>0 and a>0, $k\ge ra/(\varepsilon a+h)+r\log(\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}A/(\varepsilon a+h))$ gives error at most $(1+\varepsilon)a+h$. The paper's additional eta-independent branch is not claimed.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: Actual Gaussian/Rademacher law absolute tails have the explicit 1/(256e^2) constant and permit arbitrary real A. The indexed weak-threshold Gaussian relative/sample-size theorem requires positive trace, a nonempty average and 0<epsilon<=1. At A=0 the zero weak threshold is the full failure event; a strict-error guarantee has a separate zero-matrix reading.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Explicitly give t≥0 and the nonempty probe family.
State positive trace for the indexed weak-threshold Gaussian relative theorem; clarify the zero-matrix strict-error case.
items.informal_at_review: $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ sample complexity $m = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ for PSD $A$; Cortinovis–Kressner bounds for indefinite $A$ via Hanson–Wright.
hypotheses_at_review: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ symmetric (PSD for the Avron–Toledo bound)
$m$ i.i.d. Gaussian or Rademacher test vectors
items.conclusion_at_review: $\mathbb{P}\big[|\hat{\operatorname{tr}} - \operatorname{tr}A| \ge t\big] \le 2\exp\Big(-\tfrac{1}{256e^2}\min\Big(\tfrac{m t^2}{\|A\|_F^2}, \tfrac{m t}{\|A\|}\Big)\Big)$; for $A \succeq 0$, $m \ge 256e^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2/\delta)$ samples give relative error $\varepsilon$ with probability $1-\delta$

baseline_audit.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The law-based absolute tails agree with the explicit 1/(256e²) constant and permit arbitrary real A, a generalization of the symmetric claim. The indexed relative/sample-size endpoints are Gaussian, require positive trace and 0<ε≤1, and use a weak ≥ failure threshold. At A=0 and zero threshold that weak failure event is all samples, so positive trace must remain explicit for that endpoint; the usual strict-error guarantee treats A=0 separately.

baseline_audit.conclusion_at_review: $\mathbb{P}\big[|\hat{\operatorname{tr}} - \operatorname{tr}A| \ge t\big] \le 2\exp\Big(-\tfrac{1}{256e^2}\min\Big(\tfrac{m t^2}{\|A\|_F^2}, \tfrac{m t}{\|A\|}\Big)\Big)$; for $A \succeq 0$, $m \ge 256e^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2/\delta)$ samples give relative error $\varepsilon$ with probability $1-\delta$

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The direct second-moment endpoint proves actual diagonal-estimate unbiasedness for any isotropic vector, without zero means or independence. General variance needs centered independent unit-variance coordinates with a common finite fourth moment; its formula is sum_j A_ij^2+(m4-2)A_ii^2. Actual Gaussian/Rademacher laws discharge those hypotheses.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Add explicit centered/common-finite-fourth-moment premises for the general variance clause.
items.informal_at_review: $\mathbb{E}[z \odot Az] = \operatorname{diag}(A)$ for isotropic $z$ with independent entries; variance per coordinate.
items.conclusion_at_review: $\mathbb{E}[z \odot Az] = \operatorname{diag}(A)$, with an explicit per-coordinate variance

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The reviewed proof family separates deterministic degree<2q compression exactness from actual independent Rademacher tail bounds. The analytic ellipse parameters, Lipschitz threshold, q positivity, trace positivity and sample budget all match. The probability events use strict >, and supplied frames carry Krylov-space containment; no unproved operation count or condition-number-only analytic rate is claimed.
items.informal_at_review: Actual independent Rademacher probes combine the deterministic Lanczos compression error with the proved Hutchinson tail. General analytic rates retain the domain and magnitude parameters rho and M; relative rates require a PSD matrix function and positive trace.
hypotheses_at_review: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ has spectrum in [a,c], a<c; m>=1 probes have mutually independent Rademacher coordinates, and q>=1
For each probe z_i, $Q_i^\top Q_i=I$ and $\mathcal K_q(A,z_i)\subseteq\operatorname{range}Q_i$; $\widehat t=m^{-1}\sum_i(Q_i^\top z_i)^\top f(Q_i^\top A Q_i)(Q_i^\top z_i)$
Analytic case: $\rho>1$, F is complex-differentiable and $|F|\le M$ on the open Bernstein ellipse, and $F(t)=f(((c-a)t+c+a)/2)$ on [-1,1]. Lipschitz case: f is L-Lipschitz on [a,c]
items.conclusion_at_review: With $D_q=4nM\rho^{1-2q}/(\rho-1)$ in the analytic case or $D_q=\pi Ln(c-a)/(4q)$ in the Lipschitz case, $\mathbb P\{|\widehat t-\operatorname{tr}B|>\eta+D_q\}\le2\exp[-m(256e^2)^{-1}\min(\eta^2/\|B\|_F^2,\eta/\|B\|)]$ for eta>=0. If $D_q\le\varepsilon\tau/2$ and $m\ge1024e^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2/\delta)$, relative failure is at most delta. Analytic q may be chosen with $q\ge(1+\log(8nM/(\varepsilon\tau(\rho-1)))/\log\rho)/2$ and q>=1; a positive scalar lower bound f_min gives the computable replacement $q\ge(1+\log(8M/(\varepsilon f_{\min}(\rho-1)))/\log\rho)/2$. Absolute and Lipschitz step budgets are separate proved variants. Early Krylov termination, q above the ambient dimension and zero-size cases are included; a condition-number-only step bound is asserted only for specified functions such as the inverse.

baseline_audit.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The reviewed proof family separates deterministic degree<2q compression exactness from actual independent Rademacher tail bounds. The analytic ellipse parameters, Lipschitz threshold, q positivity, trace positivity and sample budget all match. The probability events use strict >, and supplied frames carry Krylov-space containment; no unproved operation count or condition-number-only analytic rate is claimed.
baseline_audit.informal_at_review: Actual independent Rademacher probes combine the deterministic Lanczos compression error with the proved Hutchinson tail. General analytic rates retain the domain and magnitude parameters rho and M; relative rates require a PSD matrix function and positive trace.
hypotheses_at_review: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ has spectrum in [a,c], a<c; m>=1 probes have mutually independent Rademacher coordinates, and q>=1
For each probe z_i, $Q_i^\top Q_i=I$ and $\mathcal K_q(A,z_i)\subseteq\operatorname{range}Q_i$; $\widehat t=m^{-1}\sum_i(Q_i^\top z_i)^\top f(Q_i^\top A Q_i)(Q_i^\top z_i)$
Analytic case: $\rho>1$, F is complex-differentiable and $|F|\le M$ on the open Bernstein ellipse, and $F(t)=f(((c-a)t+c+a)/2)$ on [-1,1]. Lipschitz case: f is L-Lipschitz on [a,c]
baseline_audit.conclusion_at_review: With $D_q=4nM\rho^{1-2q}/(\rho-1)$ in the analytic case or $D_q=\pi Ln(c-a)/(4q)$ in the Lipschitz case, $\mathbb P\{|\widehat t-\operatorname{tr}B|>\eta+D_q\}\le2\exp[-m(256e^2)^{-1}\min(\eta^2/\|B\|_F^2,\eta/\|B\|)]$ for eta>=0. If $D_q\le\varepsilon\tau/2$ and $m\ge1024e^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2/\delta)$, relative failure is at most delta. Analytic q may be chosen with $q\ge(1+\log(8nM/(\varepsilon\tau(\rho-1)))/\log\rho)/2$ and q>=1; a positive scalar lower bound f_min gives the computable replacement $q\ge(1+\log(8M/(\varepsilon f_{\min}(\rho-1)))/\log\rho)/2$. Absolute and Lipschitz step budgets are separate proved variants. Early Krylov termination, q above the ambient dimension and zero-size cases are included; a condition-number-only step bound is asserted only for specified functions such as the inverse.

final_review_basis.method: Final current-source signatures and preserved manual statement judgment; algorithm specification is separate from realization and cost.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The actual orthonormal-frame projected rank-k best Frobenius approximation has the stronger coefficient-one error bound, and its literal truncatedRsvdOutput wrapper gives the displayed coefficient-two corollary. This ordinary projected result does not formalize excluded Chen-Persson early-truncation identities.
items.informal_at_review: For orthonormal Q, the ordinary compressed truncated-SVD output satisfies squared Frobenius error at most the actual rank-k optimum plus the squared projection residual; in particular it satisfies the advertised bound with twice the residual.
hypotheses_at_review: A is a real finite rectangular matrix; k is any natural target rank
items.conclusion_at_review: $\|A-Q[Q^\top A]_k\|_F^2\le\mathrm{OPT}_k^2(A)+\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2\le\mathrm{OPT}_k^2(A)+2\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|_F^2$.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The actual complex bundle has both spectral and explicitly scoped Frobenius norm estimates, not one ambiguous pretty-printed norm. Full row rank supplies the head pseudoinverse and positive head filter minimum supplies inverse filter values; containing block-Krylov and empty-block cases are covered. Public raw matrix norm instances and raw frame Gram equalities remain an API-design issue under named-norm/HasOrthonormalCols standards.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Migrate these public complex signatures to specNorm/frobSq and HasOrthonormalCols in a coordinated rename/design edit, or record this outstanding design issue.
items.informal_at_review: One actual filtered-sketch competitor gives both exact squared spectral and Frobenius bounds for complex matrices. Native full row rank derives the canonical dagger expression, and the scalar envelopes and containing block Krylov specialization follow.
hypotheses_at_review: $A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ has orthogonal isometric blocks $A=U_1\Sigma_1V_1^*+U_2\Sigma_2V_2^*$, with real diagonal head and rectangular diagonal tail
$\Omega_1=V_1^*\Omega$ has full row rank, $\Omega_2=V_2^*\Omega$, and the canonical $\Omega_1^\dagger=\Omega_1^*(\Omega_1\Omega_1^*)^{-1}$
A real polynomial phi has invertible $C=\varphi(\Sigma_1^2)$; set $D=\varphi(\Sigma_2^*\Sigma_2)$ and $T=\Sigma_2D\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger C^{-1}$
P is the actual orthogonal projector onto any column space containing $\varphi(AA^*)A\Omega$; for an orthonormal Q it is $QQ^*$
items.conclusion_at_review: $\|(I-P)A\|_\xi^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|_\xi^2+\|T\|_\xi^2$ for both spectral and Frobenius norms. For k>0, $c_\varphi=\min_{i<k}|\varphi(\sigma_i^2)|>0$ and the finite tail maximum $t_\varphi$ give $\|(I-P)A\|^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|^2+(t_\varphi/c_\varphi)^2\|\Omega_2\|^2\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|^2$, with an empty tail maximum equal to zero. Every actual block Krylov range of order q satisfies these simultaneously for each degree<q filter. Real matrices and empty-block helper cases are included; k=0 uses projection contractivity.

baseline_audit.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The complex bundle genuinely contains both spectral and explicitly selected Frobenius norms; its pretty-printed declaration index erases the distinction between those instances. Full row rank derives B^*(BB^*)^−1, positive head minimum ensures inverse filter values, and the containing block-Krylov specialization is proved. Real/empty-block helpers and contractivity handle the stated boundary cases. Public matrix norms and raw orthonormality equalities in the complex files violate the current named-norm/HasOrthonormalCols design convention even though the mathematics agrees.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Migrate these public complex signatures to specNorm/frobSq and HasOrthonormalCols in a coordinated rename/design edit, or record this outstanding design issue.
baseline_audit.informal_at_review: One actual filtered-sketch competitor gives both exact squared spectral and Frobenius bounds for complex matrices. Native full row rank derives the canonical dagger expression, and the scalar envelopes and containing block Krylov specialization follow.
hypotheses_at_review: $A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ has orthogonal isometric blocks $A=U_1\Sigma_1V_1^*+U_2\Sigma_2V_2^*$, with real diagonal head and rectangular diagonal tail
$\Omega_1=V_1^*\Omega$ has full row rank, $\Omega_2=V_2^*\Omega$, and the canonical $\Omega_1^\dagger=\Omega_1^*(\Omega_1\Omega_1^*)^{-1}$
A real polynomial phi has invertible $C=\varphi(\Sigma_1^2)$; set $D=\varphi(\Sigma_2^*\Sigma_2)$ and $T=\Sigma_2D\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger C^{-1}$
P is the actual orthogonal projector onto any column space containing $\varphi(AA^*)A\Omega$; for an orthonormal Q it is $QQ^*$
baseline_audit.conclusion_at_review: $\|(I-P)A\|_\xi^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|_\xi^2+\|T\|_\xi^2$ for both spectral and Frobenius norms. For k>0, $c_\varphi=\min_{i<k}|\varphi(\sigma_i^2)|>0$ and the finite tail maximum $t_\varphi$ give $\|(I-P)A\|^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|^2+(t_\varphi/c_\varphi)^2\|\Omega_2\|^2\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|^2$, with an empty tail maximum equal to zero. Every actual block Krylov range of order q satisfies these simultaneously for each degree<q filter. Real matrices and empty-block helper cases are included; k=0 uses projection contractivity.

current_atlas_snapshot.informal: One actual filtered-sketch competitor gives both exact squared spectral and Frobenius bounds for complex matrices. Native full row rank derives the canonical dagger expression, and the scalar envelopes and containing block Krylov specialization follow.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ has orthogonal isometric blocks $A=U_1\Sigma_1V_1^*+U_2\Sigma_2V_2^*$, with real diagonal head and rectangular diagonal tail
$\Omega_1=V_1^*\Omega$ has full row rank, $\Omega_2=V_2^*\Omega$, and the canonical $\Omega_1^\dagger=\Omega_1^*(\Omega_1\Omega_1^*)^{-1}$
A real polynomial phi has invertible $C=\varphi(\Sigma_1^2)$; set $D=\varphi(\Sigma_2^*\Sigma_2)$ and $T=\Sigma_2D\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger C^{-1}$
P is the actual orthogonal projector onto any column space containing $\varphi(AA^*)A\Omega$; for an orthonormal Q it is $QQ^*$
current_atlas_snapshot.conclusion: $\|(I-P)A\|_\xi^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|_\xi^2+\|T\|_\xi^2$ for both spectral and Frobenius norms. For k>0, $c_\varphi=\min_{i<k}|\varphi(\sigma_i^2)|>0$ and the finite tail maximum $t_\varphi$ give $\|(I-P)A\|^2\le\|\Sigma_2\|^2+(t_\varphi/c_\varphi)^2\|\Omega_2\|^2\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|^2$, with an empty tail maximum equal to zero. Every actual block Krylov range of order q satisfies these simultaneously for each degree<q filter. Real matrices and empty-block helper cases are included; k=0 uses projection contractivity.

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: Actual partial Cholesky residual positivity, pivot zero rows/columns and factor-residual identities are trusted for arbitrary pivot sequences, including zero/repeated pivots, under required PSD A. The exact factor=column-Nyström identity remains a named scaffold and its generalized-Schur residual consumer depends on it.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Clarify that the dropped positivity premise concerned nonzero pivots, not the required PSD premise on A.
items.informal_at_review: For $A \succeq 0$ and pivots $S = \{s_1,\dots,s_k\}$ chosen in order, the partial Cholesky factor $F_k \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ satisfies $F_k F_k^\top = A(:,S)\,A(S,S)^{\dagger}\,A(S,:)$ (the column Nyström approximation) and the residual $A - F_k F_k^\top$ is the Schur complement of $A(S,S)$, again positive semidefinite with zero rows/columns on $S$.
hypotheses_at_review: $A \succeq 0$, any pivot sequence (zero or repeated pivots allowed; $0^{-1} = 0$)
items.conclusion_at_review: $F_k F_k^\top = A(:,S) A(S,S)^\dagger A(S,:)$; residual $= A / A(S,S) \succeq 0$

items.mathematical_and_correspondence_review: The actual existence theorem selects distinct columns with identity interpolation and coefficients bounded by one, and gives spectral error at most sqrt(1+k*(n-k))*sigma_k in the library's zero-based singular-value convention, under k<=rank A. The actual rank-sized selection reconstructs A exactly, including rank zero and empty labels. The proof uses the existing genuine strong-RRQR existence theorem; a computable coefficient-two algorithm does not follow from pure existence.
recommended_atlas_repairs: Keep the computable-choice clause separate from maximum-volume existence unless algorithm realization is supplied.
items.informal_at_review: For $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ of rank $k$ there are $k$ columns $J$ and $T \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ with $A = A(:,J)\, T$, $T(:,J) = I$ and $|t_{ij}| \le 1$ (choose $J$ maximising the volume of $A(:,J)$); for general $A$, $\|A - A(:,J) T\| \le \sqrt{1 + k(n-k)}\,\sigma_{k+1}(A)$ with $|t_{ij}| \le 1$ (and $|t_{ij}| \le 2$ for a computable choice).
items.conclusion_at_review: $A \approx A(:,J)\,T$ with $T(:,J) = I$, $|t_{ij}| \le 1$, error $\le \sqrt{1+k(n-k)}\,\sigma_{k+1}$

    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ A.rank) :
    ∃ e : Fin k ↪ n, ∃ T : Matrix (Fin k) n ℝ,
